key_insight: Reasoning-Trace Analysis makes LLM-generated Q-matrix assignments inspectable, revealing disagreements that matrix-level agreement and fit alone cannot explain.
engineering_relevance: AI-assisted assessment pipelines can use trace analysis to audit item–skill mappings alongside expert review and empirical validation.
method: Prompt LLMs to generate attribute-labeled reasoning steps.
Reconstruct item–attribute assignments from those steps.
Compare Q-matrices and inspect traces to investigate disagreements.
evidence_signal: Across four LLMs, an empirical study of 11 fraction-subtraction items and 536 examinees, with 100 replications per condition, found mean reference overlap of .809 for trace-derived matrices versus .877 for directly generated matrices.
watch_item: Trace-derived matrices varied more across replications, and their inspectability does not establish that generated explanations faithfully reflect model reasoning.
paper_title: Reasoning-Trace Analysis Using Large Language Models for Interpretable Q-Matrix Construction
